question.:question/problem: At which point on the curve $8 x y + 4 y^{2}=- 4 x^{2} + 5 y - 30$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$\begin{aligned}8 x y + 4 y^{2}&=- 4 x^{2} + 5 y - 30\\4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30&=0\end{aligned}$$

If we set $f(x,y)=4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$t(x,y)=f_y(x,y)\,i-f_x(x,y)\,j$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)&=\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(4 x^{2} + 8 x y + 4 y^{2} - 5 y + 30)\,j\\&=(8 x + 8 y - 5)\,i-(8 x + 8 y)\,j\end{aligned}$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j&=0\\- 8 x - 8 y&=0\\y&=-x\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $y=-x$ into the equation of our curve gives:

$$\begin{aligned}4(x+(-x))^{2}-5(-x)-(-30)&=0\\5x-(-30)&=0\\5x&=-30\\x&=-6\end{aligned}$$

Finally, the corresponding point is $(-6,6)$.
